model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 weighted average diluted shares for FFO/Core Operating Earnings (187.190M), which includes exchangeable operating-partnership units (period-end: 183.118M common + 3.838M OP units = 186.956M at 30-Jun-26). Held flat: SBC (incl. equity-award withholding) is expensed in the flow. The 2025 step-up in OP units (1.10M -> 3.84M) was acquisition currency, already in the count.
inputs.debt_memo: Held at zero in the engine: Core Operating Earnings/AFFO are already after interest expense AND preferred dividends, so the debt and preferreds are charged in the flow. Actual pro-rata position at 30-Jun-26 (Q2-26 supplemental, capitalization table): outstanding debt $5,443.7M, cash $191.6M, preferred stock $225.0M (6.25% Series A $115M + 5.875% Series B $110M liquidation preference) -> net debt and preferred $5,477.1M; 5.0x Operating EBITDAre; fixed-charge cover 4.2x; ~$1.5B revolver capacity. Do NOT deduct a second time.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Q4 earnings release (8-K 2026-02-05, ex99.1) COE-to-AFFO reconciliation: SBC added back $21.648M; plus $6.794M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement (cash-flow statement, kpis equity_award_taxes). The company's AFFO adds SBC back; the house basis deducts SBC + withholding once.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2025 or H1-2026 per the extracted cash-flow lines; $200.1M repurchased in FY2024. The flat count is a modelling convention REG funds through ATM/OP-unit issuance and occasional buybacks, not a steady repurchase programme.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the flow is post-interest and post-preferred. 9.25% = 10-year UST ~5.24% (2026-10-01) + 0.8 beta x 5.0% ERP. Grocery-anchored A-/A3 shopping-centre REIT: more defensive than general retail, more cyclical than self-storage (PSA/MAA at 9.0%), in line with net-lease O at 9.5%. +/-50bp on CoE is roughly +/-9% on base IV; the Treasury print is the single biggest lever.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable as a lessee; REG is the lessor. Ground leases are inside property operating expense and therefore inside Core Operating Earnings.
inputs.nci_treatment: Core Operating Earnings/AFFO are pro-rata: consolidated entities plus REG's share of unconsolidated JVs, net of the share attributable to noncontrolling interests. Exchangeable OP units are in the share count, so their income is in the flow. NCI charged once.
inputs.engine_mapping: Engine 'revenue' = consolidated total revenue (FY2025 $1,553.5M, scaling denominator only). Engine 'EBITDA margin' = (Core Operating Earnings + debt-cost/derivative add-back + SBC) / revenue: FY2025 ($813.249M + $9.074M + $21.648M) / $1,553.524M = 54.33%. sbc_pct = SBC + equity-award withholding / revenue (1.83%). capex_pct = operating capital expenditures (TI, leasing commissions, building improvements; FY2025 $137.3M = 8.84%) PLUS the equity-funded share of development/redevelopment spend (see notes). D&A, cash tax and working capital are zero: COE is already a cash-like REIT earnings measure (straight-line and above/below-market rents stripped), REIT taxes are immaterial and inside COE. FY0 check: 54.33 - 1.83 - 8.84 = 43.66% x 1,553.5 = $678.2M = last_fcf.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity via the component engine, per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing (REIT -> AFFO/distributable-profit capitalisation at CoE, never subtract net debt afterwards). First valuation of REG (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Same pattern as MAA, PSA and O. Growth paths are AGGREGATE (not per-share) Core Operating Earnings growth on a flat 187.19M count and INCLUDE development-driven NOI; to avoid counting growth without paying for it, capex carries the equity-funded share of development spend (FY2026 guide ~$350M development/redevelopment spend, ~$1B of starts targeted over 2026-28; ~55% equity-funded after leverage-neutral debt at 5x on a ~9% yield -> ~11% of revenue in FY2026, tapering to ~2.3% by year 10 as the programme shrinks relative to the rent roll). Year 1 = FY2026 anchored to raised guidance: COE $4.62-$4.66/diluted share x ~187.0M = ~$868M (+6.7% aggregate over FY2025's $813.2M, of which ~2.2% is the 2025 share/OP-unit issuance already in the count). FY2026 is three-quarters elapsed but discounted a full year (house end-of-year convention). Q2-2026 is not yet in Metrics.csv (XBRL feed ends at Q1-2026); H1-2026 COE $434.3M / AFFO $382.9M taken from the Q2-26 earnings 8-K. GAAP EPS and P/E are meaningless here (depreciation and property-sale gains); Analysis.json had a JSON syntax error (missing brace, line 80) which was repaired so it parses.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (3.5%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (8.9%). Revenue is inflated by the stock-funded Urstadt Biddle merger (Aug-2023) and acquisitions paid in OP units; book equity is depressed by real-estate depreciation. Neither is a REIT growth proxy -- per-share Core Operating Earnings is.
historical_growth.notes: EPS column is NULL in XBRL for this filer and GAAP EPS is not meaningful for a REIT. Owner AFFO = company AFFO - SBC - equity-award withholding (FY2023 612.2-17.3-7.7; FY2024 649.4-18.5-19.5; FY2025 706.6-21.6-6.8); only three years pulled, so 3/5yr FCF CAGRs are null. Owner-AFFO growth (7.5%) runs ahead of per-share COE growth (4.8%) because the share count rose ~5.6% with the UBP merger.

base.margin_rationale: FY2026 implied (COE mid $868M + ~$9.5M debt-cost add-back + ~$24M SBC) / ~$1,662M revenue = 54.2%. Held flat: occupancy commencement (leased 96.9% vs commenced 94.5%) and expense recovery lift NOI margin, offset by refinancing $5.4B of debt at ~4.5% WAIR into a higher-rate market.
base.capex_rationale: Operating capex 8.7% of revenue (FY2025 8.8%, H1-26 $67.9M) + equity-funded development 11.3% in FY2026 tapering to 2.3% by year 10.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at the raised guidance midpoint (COE ~$4.64/share, same-property NOI +3.7-4.1%). The ~240bp leased-vs-commenced gap closes over 2027-28, cash leasing spreads settle from ~10% toward high single digits, and the $680M in-process pipeline (80% leased, ~9% yield) delivers on schedule, so aggregate COE grows 5-5.5% in 2027-28 before fading to rent-escalator growth (2.5%) as development shrinks relative to the rent roll. Refinancing ~4.5%-coupon debt into a ~5.5-6% market absorbs the operating leverage from occupancy, holding the COE margin flat. Development is paid for: the equity-funded share is deducted every year.
scenario_narratives.bull: Near-zero new shopping-centre supply keeps pricing power intact: cash spreads stay double-digit, occupancy pushes past prior peaks, and the ~$1B 2026-28 starts programme is executed and extended at ~9% yields well above the ~6% cap rates the market pays for grocery-anchored centres. Rates ease or credit spreads stay tight, so refinancing is benign and the COE margin widens ~1.3pp. Aggregate COE compounds 6-6.5% through 2028 and ~4-5% to 2031, with a 3.0% terminal rent growth for an infill, supply-constrained portfolio.
scenario_narratives.bear: Occupancy mean-reverts from a 96.9%-leased peak: a grocer bankruptcy or consolidation (Kroger/Albertsons-style store rationalisation, ~20% of ABR from grocers) and shop-space tenant failures in a consumer slowdown reverse the commencement tailwind; spreads compress to low single digits. Higher-for-longer rates reprice $5.4B of debt and $225M of callable preferreds, compressing the COE margin ~1.5pp by 2030, and development starts are cut back (lower capex, lower growth). FY2026 still delivers near guidance (three quarters done), then aggregate COE growth slows to ~2-3%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the portfolio is at a cyclical occupancy peak, so the downside case is mean reversion of the very metric driving current growth, not a solvency event (A-/A3, 5.0x, 4.2x fixed-charge cover). Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice and FY2026 is three-quarters complete. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs two independent things -- sustained double-digit spreads AND a benign rate/refinancing path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Regency is valued as a stream of house-basis AFFO to common (Core Operating Earnings less operating capex, SBC and equity-award withholding), capitalised at a 9.25% cost of equity. Debt and preferreds are inside the flow, so nothing is deducted afterwards. Growth includes development, and the equity-funded share of development spend is deducted, so growth is never counted without being paid for.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: the 10-year Treasury at ~5.24% drives the 9.25% CoE; +/-50bp moves base IV by roughly +/-9%.
Occupancy at a cyclical peak (96.9% leased): the commencement tailwind in 2026-27 reverses if a major grocer or shop-space cohort fails.
Refinancing: ~$5.4B of pro-rata debt at ~4.5% WAIR rolls into higher coupons; each +100bp on a year's ~$600M of maturities costs ~$6M of COE.
Development yield vs. cost of capital: the bull case depends on ~9% yields holding against construction-cost inflation.
Year 1 is discounted a full year although FY2026 is three-quarters elapsed (house convention), a slight understatement.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 66.86-83.66
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL (Metrics.csv through Q1-2026); Core Operating Earnings, AFFO, operating capex and SBC add-back from earnings 8-K ex99.1 for Q4-2023, Q4-2024, Q4-2025 and Q2-2026 (Extracted/REG_8K_*.txt); capitalization table, preferreds and development spend from the Q2-2026 Quarterly Supplemental (8-K 2026-07-29 ex99.2).
data_sources.screen: info.json stockanalysis.com snapshot 2026-09-22 (P/E 24.57 is GAAP and not meaningful for a REIT).
